title: Demystifying Prompt Stealing Attacks against Synthetic Video
abstract: arXiv:2611.00102v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Creators publicly showcase generated content to advertise and sell their work, but these examples may also enable unauthorized reproduction and customization. We study whether an adversary can derive reusable inputs from a single public video for faithful reconstruction and controlled editing, without access to the original prompt or generator. We adapt captioning and prompt optimization approaches to video prompt stealing attacks (PSAs) and find that prompt recovery alone provides limited reconstruction fidelity. Even the original prompt produces different spatial and temporal realizations when the initial noise changes. Using an independent generator enlarges the reconstruction gap, as reusing the original prompt and seed can still produce substantially different videos. We propose V-PSA, which uses a recovered caption and DDIM inversion to construct a reference trajectory under an independent generator. Null-Text Inversion t

translated_title: 揭秘针对合成视频的提示窃取攻击
translated_abstract: 创作者公开展示生成的内容以宣传和销售其作品，但这些示例也可能使未经授权的复制和定制成为可能。我们研究攻击者是否能够在无法访问原始提示或生成器的情况下，仅凭单个公开视频推导出可重用的输入，以实现忠实重建和受控编辑。我们将字幕生成和提示优化方法适配到视频提示窃取攻击（PSA）中，发现仅靠提示恢复只能提供有限的重建保真度——即使使用原始提示，当初始噪声改变时也会产生不同的空间和时间表现。使用独立的生成器会进一步扩大重建差距，因为即使重用原始提示和种子，仍可能生成截然不同的视频。我们提出V-PSA，该方法利用恢复的字幕和DDIM反演在独立生成器下构建参考轨迹，并通过Null-Text反演……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究提出V-PSA方法，证明单纯恢复文本提示无法忠实重建合成视频，通过结合恢复的字幕与DDIM反演构建参考轨迹，实现对公开合成视频的高保真重建与受控编辑。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes V-PSA, which combines recovered captions with DDIM inversion to construct reference trajectories, enabling high-fidelity reconstruction and controlled editing of publicly shared synthetic videos beyond mere prompt recovery.
